chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a person in Ihram who catches prey, he (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the expiation.' I said, 'And if he catches another?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he catches another, there is no expiation upon him, and he is among those for whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: And whoever returns (to it), Allah will inflict retribution on him.'

key_terms.الْكَفَّارَةُ: Expiation or compensation (usually involving feeding the poor or sacrificing an animal)
key_terms.صَيْداً: Game or hunted prey (specifically land animals)
key_terms.عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic (an honorific title for Allah)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: A person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on expiation for a pilgrim who catches multiple game animals while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of repeated hunting during Ihram, establishing that while the initial catch triggers a specific expiation (kaffarah), subsequent catches do not accumulate additional penalties. The reasoning relies on the Quranic principle that Allah's retribution suffices for those who persist in the transgression, reflecting the Shia scholarly view on the sufficiency of divine justice over cumulative ritual penalties in this context.
